key_insight: The paper teaches LLMs to generate feasible MILP instances that are not just correct, but intentionally hard for solvers by using solver feedback as the reward.
engineering_relevance: This can produce stronger benchmarks for optimization research and more challenging training data for solver-oriented learning systems without needing seed MILP instances.
method: Use a challenger-solver asymmetric self-play setup where the LLM proposes instances and the solver returns feasibility and hardness feedback.
Reward instances using solver-stage signals such as branch-and-bound node counts and post-cut relaxation gaps, rather than binary correctness alone.
Fine-tune Gemma-4-12B and Qwen3.5-4B with GRPO plus a size curriculum to obtain OptiScribe-12B and OptiScribe-4B.
evidence_signal: On capacitated facility location and max-cut, the models increase median SCIP search nodes by 1.7-5x for OptiScribe-12B and up to 15.6x for OptiScribe-4B, while also improving feasibility rates on facility location by 9-19 points.
watch_item: The approach depends on solver-in-the-loop feedback and specific hardness metrics, so reward design and solver choice may affect transferability across problem families and sizes.
paper_title: Teaching LLMs to Generate Challenging MILP Instances via Solver Feedback
